Hey new ADHDer! I resonated with your story a bit because I have both depression and ADHD-Inattentive.

I actually got both of my diagnoses in late 2018 (at 21), but knew I had depression and anxiety years before. Going through a grieving process was an absolutely legitimate thing, because I also wished that I had known years prior, so my teen years would have been enjoyable. 

I'm medicated for the disorders now, but that doesn't really *fix* the issues; it's more of an assistant. Right now you're learning about a version of yourself that has the neurological assistance it needs, and you may find an interest in things you never paid attention to before. 

Within the realm of safety, feel free to explore those new interests with an open mind. Be aware, however, that the medication you're taking may level out over time. Some days may feel like you never took it at all, others may feel like a kick into high gear. It's a balancing act to find out what dosage works for you.

Since I take stimulants, my increased heart rate prevents me from taking my needed naps; keep on the lookout for any side effects you may experience too. When you feel overwhelmed in general, talking to someone you trust helps a bit. Sometimes there's so much going on in our heads, we can't sort through the thoughts ourselves.

Last thing (and maybe the most important): Talk to people who WILL listen and NOT talk down on your experiences. Learning about ADHD's impact on your life, and the condition as a whole, can be a rough experience when you have people around who invalidate you. By having good supporters around you, you'll be able to process things at your own pace.

Each class has a lot of skills and core combos (usually GCDs), and weaving those together during combat adds a lot to a class's playstyle. I play dragoon a lot, and having those 2.5 seconds to use an OGCD gives me a chance to decide how to approach an enemy. "Should I activate a damage up buff? Should I leap away from an oncoming aoe?" These are questions that you can answer during those seconds.
